key_insight: GA-AMNO separates adaptive PDE computation into two readable parts: physics-informed node placement for "where to compute" and gauge-aware feature transport for "how to interact" across changing meshes.
engineering_relevance: This helps scientific machine learning models remain accurate and interpretable under nonuniform discretizations, especially when mesh changes create representation mismatch across locations.
method: Physics-informed adaptive mesh allocation chooses computation sites based on local PDE structure.
Geometry-conditioned low-rank gauge transport maps source features into the target node's representation context before aggregation.
Operator readability enables controlled interventions to test the roles of allocation and interaction separately.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experiments on five PDE benchmarks, with improved predictive accuracy plus geometric-mismatch analyses and interventions validating the allocation and transport roles.
watch_item: Gauge transport and mesh adaptation may add implementation complexity, and the continuity guarantees rely on topology-preserving mesh deformations.
paper_title: Where to Compute and How to Interact: Operator-Readable Adaptation with Gauge-Aware Transport
